This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It
ends with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this
page has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary digital-media multimedia elemental-tetrad mechanics aesthetics player-experience feedback asset production-pipeline pre-production >}}

## 1.1 What digital media are

- **Digital media:** text, images, audio, video, animation and interactive
  content, stored as numbers.
- A work with several types is **multimedia**. The game itself is
  **interactive media**.
- Images: a **raster** image is a grid of pixels (photos, painted art);
  **vector** graphics are shapes that stay sharp at any size (logos,
  buttons).
- One level of *Lantern Keeper*: a line of text, the painted forest, piano
  music and a chime, a short scene of the village, and the taps of the
  player.

![The media of one game screen.](images/annotated-screen.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The rules that answer the player are a medium too: interactive media.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Six types in your game"}
Choose a game on your phone. Write one example of each of the six types of
media from this game.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "Text: the names of the cards. Images: the
characters. Audio: the music of the menu. Video: the intro scene.
Animation: the hero running. Interactive media: the game reacts to my
taps."

- ☐ Six different types.
- ☐ A real example from the game for each.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Types of media"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="text|animation"}
A cut-scene between two levels.
:   video

    Why: A cut-scene is moving pictures that the player watches.

The game logo, for a tiny icon and a big poster.
:   vector

    Why: Vector shapes stay sharp at any size.

A painted forest background with soft light.
:   raster

    Why: A painting with many colours is a grid of pixels.

Several media types together in one work.
:   multimedia

    Why: Multimedia combines several types.
:::
:::

## 1.2 The game as a composite medium

- The **elemental tetrad** (Schell): **mechanics** (rules), **story**
  (events), **aesthetics** (look, sound, feel), **technology** (device,
  engine, screen).
- All four are equally important. Media succeed when they make the planned
  **player experience** stronger.
- *Tide Runner*: swipe to jump waves (mechanics); bring medicine before the
  storm (story); bright colours and steel drums (aesthetics); a phone in
  landscape at 60 fps (technology): *fast and joyful*.

![The elemental tetrad.](images/tetrad.png){width=62%}

{{< sim file="sims/juice-it.html" poster="sims/juice-it.png" title="Juice It: same mechanics, different media" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Aesthetics are not only graphics: sound, music, vibration and rhythm count
too.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Juice It"}
In **Juice It**, play 30 seconds with all media layers off, then switch them
on one at a time. Write one word for the experience at the start and one at
the end, and the layer that changed it most.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "At the start: boring. At the end: exciting. The
sound effects changed it most, because every jump and star now gives
feedback." The rules stayed the same; only the media changed the
experience.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The tetrad"}
Choose the element of the tetrad. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="player experience"}
Swipe up to jump over a wave.
:   mechanics

    Why: It is a rule: what the player can do.

The surfer must bring medicine before the storm.
:   story

    Why: These are the events of the game.

Bright sea colours and steel-drum music.
:   aesthetics

    Why: How the game looks and sounds.

Simple water effects so that old phones keep 60 fps.
:   technology

    Why: The device and the engine limit what is possible.

A vibration of the phone when the surfer falls.
:   aesthetics

    Why: Aesthetics include what the player feels, not only sees.
:::
:::

## 1.3 The jobs of game media

- **Feedback:** what happened? **Guidance:** where to go? **Mood:** how
  should it feel? **Story:** what is happening? **Identity:** which game is
  this?
- One element often has several jobs: the splash of *Tide Runner* is
  feedback (the jump worked), mood (fresh, joyful) and identity.
- Explain, do not only describe: the element, its job, its effect on the
  player.

![One coin, three jobs.](images/media-functions.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"There is music in the menu" only describes. Say what the music does to the
player.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Sound off"}
Play a game you know for one minute with the sound off. Which sound is
missing, and what was its job? How does the game help a player who cannot
hear?

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "The hit sound is missing: its job is feedback,
so I do not notice when I lose health. The game also flashes the screen
red, so a player who cannot hear still gets the feedback."

- ☐ A real sound and its job.
- ☐ One other channel (a flash, a vibration) that does the same job.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Which job?"}
Choose the function. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="technology|pre-production"}
A chime and a flash when the player collects a coin.
:   feedback

    Why: It tells the player what the action did.

A glowing door at the end of a dark room.
:   guidance

    Why: It shows the player where to go.

Slow music in a sad scene.
:   mood

    Why: It sets how the moment should feel.

A theme tune that players know at once.
:   identity

    Why: It tells which game this is.

A broken statue in an old village.
:   story

    Why: It tells what happened here, without words.
:::
:::

## 1.4 The creative production pipeline

- **Pre-production:** plan: the idea, story, script, storyboard, style
  guide, time plan, budget.
- **Production:** make the **assets**: draw, animate, compose, record,
  film.
- **Post-production:** edit, mix, correct, export (PNG for pictures, Ogg
  for sounds), then **test**: testing can send work back.
- This course: story and scripts (lectures 2–4), storyboards (5–6), sound,
  music and video (7–11), intellectual property (12–13).

![The production pipeline.](images/pipeline.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Start with a plan: without pre-production, assets do not fit together.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Make one small asset"}
Make a coin icon: write a one-line plan, draw it in Paint, and save it as
a PNG with a clear name such as `icon_coin_v1.png`.

::: {.check}
A good result: a one-line plan that says the shape, the colour and where
the icon is used; a simple drawing that follows it; and a file such as
`icon_coin_v1.png`, whose name says what the asset is and its version.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Which stage?"}
Choose the stage of the pipeline. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="testing only"}
Writing the script of a cut-scene.
:   pre-production

    Why: The script is part of the plan.

Recording the voice of the hero.
:   production

    Why: Recording makes an asset.

Mixing the music so that voices stay clear.
:   post-production

    Why: Mixing finishes the assets.

Drawing the storyboard.
:   pre-production

    Why: The storyboard plans the pictures before they are made.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Lantern Keeper's media plan {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The *Lantern Keeper* team must plan its media: a **2-minute music loop**, a
**firefly chime with three variations**, a **logo** for the store page, a
**painted forest background** and a **30-second trailer**. The story: the
spirit must **light the village lanterns before sunrise**. First play the
game, and switch each element of the tetrad off once.

{{< sim file="sims/lantern-keeper.html" poster="sims/lantern-keeper.png" title="Lantern Keeper: switch the tetrad on and off" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Planning the media (harder)"}
Lantern Keeper's plan: a music loop, a chime with three variations, a logo,
a painted background, a trailer; the story: light the lanterns before
sunrise. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="pre-production|mechanics"}
"Light the lanterns before sunrise": which element of the tetrad?
:   story

    Why: It is the events of the game.

Why does the chime have three variations instead of one?
:   so that it does not repeat exactly

    Why: The same sound again and again soon annoys the player.

Which image type for the logo, on a tiny icon and a big banner?
:   vector

    Why: Shapes stay sharp at every size.

Which image type for the painted forest background?
:   raster

    Why: A painting with soft light is a grid of pixels.

In which stage is the trailer edited and exported?
:   post-production

    Why: Editing and exporting finish an asset.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Digital media are text, images, audio, video, animation and interactive
  content stored as numbers.
- The tetrad: mechanics, story, aesthetics and technology make the player
  experience together.
- Media do five jobs: feedback, guidance, mood, story and identity.
- The pipeline: pre-production, production, post-production, then testing.
